source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. The Gupta Dynasty
points: The **Gupta Empire** (c. 320–550 CE) ruled much of north India from **Pataliputra**.

sub: **Chandragupta I** — first great Gupta king; took the title **Maharajadhiraja**.
**Samudragupta** — a great conqueror; his deeds are recorded in the **Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription)** by the poet **Harishena**.
**Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)** — defeated the **Shakas**; the Chinese pilgrim **Fa-Hien (Faxian)** visited in his reign.

points: Later kings (**Kumaragupta, Skandagupta**) faced **Huna** invasions, which weakened the empire.

sections.heading: 2. A 'Golden Age' of Creativity
points: Often called the **Classical / Golden Age** of Indian culture for its achievements in **literature, science, art and mathematics**.
**Literature:** **Kalidasa** (Abhijnana-shakuntalam, Meghaduta) wrote in Sanskrit.
The **decimal system** and the concept of **zero (shunya)** were developed/used — a lasting gift to the world.

sections.heading: 3. Science and Learning
points: **Aryabhata** — astronomer-mathematician; explained that the **Earth rotates on its axis**, worked on the value of **π**, and eclipses.
**Varahamihira** — astronomy (Brihat Samhita); **Sushruta and Charaka** — medicine and surgery.
**Nalanda** (and other centres) became famous seats of learning.

sections.heading: 4. Art and Architecture
points: **Temple architecture** developed (early structural temples, e.g. **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh**).
Superb **sculpture** and **paintings** — the finest at the **Ajanta caves** (Buddhist).
Fine **gold coins** depicting kings and deities.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Guptas c. 320–550 CE; capital Pataliputra; 'Golden/Classical Age'.
Samudragupta = Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad pillar), poet Harishena.
Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' defeated the Shakas; Fa-Hien (Faxian) visited.
Kalidasa (literature); Aryabhata (Earth rotates, π, zero/decimal); Varahamihira, Sushruta, Charaka.
Ajanta paintings; Huna invasions weakened the empire.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Prayaga Prashasti** praises **Samudragupta** and was composed by **Harishena**.
**Chandragupta II** (not I) took the title **Vikramaditya** and defeated the **Shakas**; **Fa-Hien** visited in his reign.
**Aryabhata** proposed that the **Earth rotates** — an early scientific insight.
The Gupta age is the **'Classical/Golden Age'**; **Ajanta** paintings belong here.
